A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same weighted decentralized gradient-tracking study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original noisy least-squares experiments and ResNet-18 training on CIFAR-10, including convergence curves, test accuracies, and computed spectral gaps in Section 8 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds larger-network experiments and distance-to-optimum measurements in Section 8 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The weighted GT updates and mixing-matrix construction remain unchanged. Algorithm 6 makes a limited pseudocode correction: initial degree deficits become max{0, d_i−deg(i)} instead of d_i−deg(i), retaining the same positive-deficit edge-selection and stopping rules.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic isotropic least-squares optimization and CIFAR-10 classification using the same topology families. Added network sizes, weight vectors, and partition imbalance vary configurations within this retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons remain Strategy I versus Strategy II. The larger-network experiments extend these same comparators; newly cited algorithms are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 expands least-squares settings from 16 to 16/32/64 nodes and CIFAR-10 to 32 nodes, introduces more imbalanced weight vectors, and adds distance-to-optimum evaluation. The new CIFAR-10 curves cover 2,000 iterations versus 2,500 for retained settings. Appendix F.3 also revises A_i=ζ_i I to A_i=√ζ_i I while retaining the gradient formula; this establishes a specification correction, not evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 and Figure 6 add a focused diagnostic testing whether both strategies approach the same optimum and comparing their residual errors. Larger-network experiments also extend robustness evidence under stronger weight imbalance, although network size and imbalance change together.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging ten seeds for least-squares and six for CIFAR-10, with the same composite noise-seed rule. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practice are introduced.

E6.justification: The original 16-node plots and spectral-gap entries are retained. v4 adds larger-network convergence and classification results, distance-to-optimum curves, and spectral-gap entries: for example, the tailored 32-node graph reports 0.343 for W versus 0.040 for W_ds. These are additional results under new configurations, not improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 7.2 replaces the incorrect unnormalized quadratic form with a weighted Dirichlet form, and v4 adds ε≥1/2 for the spectral-gap reformulation. Corollary 7.3 and its proof are substantially replaced by a centered Rayleigh-quotient comparison and a different sufficient edge condition. Theorem 7.1 replaces fixed η=0.1 with a derived constant, while Appendix C corrects missing factors and summation terms in the convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the claim of a shared expected descent direction with the more precise claim that both strategies target the same weighted objective, and explicitly describe weights as prescribed and fixed. The three principal contributions concerning weighted-space analysis, penalty factors, and topology design remain.

C2.justification: Remark 6.6 explicitly limits the comparison to standard single-loop GT and disclaims universal minimax or lower-bound conclusions; Section 9 adds directed-graph and optimality limitations. The topology interpretation also changes substantially: v2's spectral-gap maximization claim becomes a narrower minimum-edge-coefficient guarantee requiring an additional edge condition.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the new weight vectors and tailored-graph degree sequences, clarifies that weights remain fixed across seeds and topology comparisons, and explains the additional scalar communication required by weighted mixing. Conversely, it removes the explicit least-squares step size α=0.12 supplied in v2, reducing reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related work adds bilevel optimization and Markovian sampling references, including Kong et al. (2025) and Sun et al. (2023), while new motivation cites additional weighted-learning literature. Fan (1949) is removed. The main positioning relative to diffusion, exact diffusion, and directed-network optimization remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v4 revises aggregate-dynamics and interpretation passages, adds motivation and consensus exposition in the appendices, and introduces explicit limitations and acknowledgments. Existing appendix material is largely retained under shifted lettering.

P2.justification: The separate CIFAR-10 figures become a full-width Figure 3 combining retained panels with a new 32-node row. v4 also adds larger-network least-squares, distance-to-optimum, and 32-node classification figures, and restructures Table 1 into network-size blocks. Existing adjacency diagrams and 16-node appendix plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs an important deficiency in the central topology argument: the transformed Laplacian and its quadratic form are corrected, and the comparison accounts for the different orthogonality constraints in Theorem 7.2 and Corollary 7.3. Clearer applicability limits and additional convergence diagnostics further strengthen the paper. These substantive gains outweigh the limited reproducibility regression from omitting the least-squares step size.
